item.title: Health Minister calls for stronger PHAs
item.description: Health Minister, Dr. Billy Joseph is calling for stronger Provincial Health Authorities (PHA), greater accountability and better health outcomes as PNG marks 20 years of PHA reforms. Dr Billy Joseph made the call while officially opening the 60th Papua New Guinea Medical Symposium at the PNG University of Technology in Lae this week.
item.content:encoded:
Health Minister, Dr. Billy Joseph is calling for stronger Provincial Health Authorities (PHA), greater accountability and better health outcomes as PNG marks 20 years of PHA reforms.

Dr Billy Joseph made the call while officially opening the 60th Papua New Guinea Medical Symposium at the PNG University of Technology in Lae this week.

The theme is “Provincial Health Authorities Establishment Review: Past, Present and Future — PHAs Forward and Back.”

He says PNG now has more health facilities, health workers and investment which has grown from K346 million in 2007 to more than K3.2 billion in 2026, but key health indicators have not improved at the same pace.

Dr Joseph said skilled births remain at 44 percent, routine immunization is below 50 percent for some vaccines, tuberculosis (TB) rates are above 400 per 100,000, and around 1,256 health facilities remain closed.

He outlined a 120-Day Plan with 10 priorities including stronger leadership, medical supply reform, health infrastructure, workforce strengthening and a national pre-hospital care system.

The Minister stressed that PHA Boards and CEOs must be held accountable, with performance measured by results delivered to patients and communities.

Dr Joseph said the PHA review must lead to action to build a stronger, more accountable health system for the next 50 years of PNG.

item.title: Teachers bear brunt of Madang El Nino crisis

item.content:encoded:
Teachers and their families in Madang are bearing the brunt of the worsening El Niño-induced dry spell as schools across the province struggle to operate without basic water supplies and an official provincial action plan.

The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] in Madang has raised serious concerns over the welfare of educators, stating that prolonged heat and severe water shortages in rural schools are threatening both lives and learning.

Acting Provincial TSC Advisor Kenneth Kalai expressed deep concern for non-local teachers posted to remote areas who are currently struggling for basic survival.

"I am particularly concerned about my teachers and their families. Most of them are not from the local communities," Kalai said.

"Some of the schools they are teaching in, especially those in the rural areas, do not have water catchments. They use creeks and rivers to source their supply of water, and some of these water sources have dried up."

Kalai revealed that teachers are being forced to walk long distances to cart water for basic household and daily needs. The hardship has been compounded by rising local tensions over dwindling natural reserves.

"My concern is about the welfare of my teachers and their families because some local people are now restricting them from accessing the water sources. They are even charging them fees," he said.

Despite a meeting held by the Madang Provincial Education Board last month to address the crisis, local school administrators report a lack of clear directives from provincial authorities.

"The heat is unbearable, and the least the province should do is come up with a disaster management plan," Kalai said. "The silence in the province is deafening. Responsible authorities are not talking about El Niño."

In the absence of a provincial relief framework, the provincial education director has directed head teachers across Madang to monitor conditions daily and submit weekly situational reports.

Taking early emergency measures, the Madang Inspectorate approved temporary schedule changes for schools in Zones 2 and 3, covering the Ambenob and Transgogol local level government [LLG] areas.

While applauding the inspectorate’s proactive stance to protect staff and students from heat exhaustion, Kalai urged all provincial stakeholders to take immediate structural action before the situation turns fatal.

"We can't wait until someone dies," Kalai said.

item.title: Brothers complete 3500km walk across PNG for children with cancer
item.description: 130-day journey from Bougainville to Vanimo to fund hospital. Two brothers, Mel-Kizenderk and Kormson Nili, have walked 3,500 kilometers across half of Papua New Guinea to raise funds and awareness for children living with cancer.
item.content:encoded:
130-day journey from Bougainville to Vanimo to fund hospital.

Two brothers, Mel-Kizenderk and Kormson Nili, have walked 3,500 kilometers across half of Papua New Guinea to raise funds and awareness for children living with cancer.

The walk began in Bougainville on 14th November 2025 and ended 130 days later on 27th August 2026 at the Wutung Border Post in Vanimo, West Sepik.

Hailing from East New Britain and Enga, the brothers took on the challenge to address child cancer, a growing health concern in PNG.

According to the World Health Organisation, approximately 140 children are diagnosed with cancer every year in Papua New Guinea. WHO estimates the real number could be 400 or more, based on the country’s youth population.

At the Children’s Cancer Ward at Port Moresby General Hospital, there are only 12 beds to serve children since the ward opened in 2015.

“1000 children every year is not a small imaginary number, and with 12 beds in POMGEN, the numbers are alarming. This is based on global WHO averages from 200 other countries. Our country does not have reliable data, not even for census to begin with,” Mel said.

At every stop in communities, markets, schools and churches, the brothers shared messages on cancer signs, possible causes, and prevention, hoping to save at least one life.

Through the walk they also saw the urgent need for better health facilities in remote areas.

“It is the rural areas that are most difficult to reach. Main reasons being lack of education, language barriers and strong superstitious beliefs. This could be the main reason most children in those areas are suffering and dying from cancer, but the data is not being collected,” Mel said.

The brothers say they hope to bring to the attention of every citizen in PNG, especially leaders, that this long-neglected disease is killing thousands of children across the country’s 22 provinces.

“We walk so more children can get a bed. We walk so more lives can be saved,” he said.

All funds raised through their 'Walk for Kids with Cancer' GoFundMe page will be used to purchase more beds and medication for the children’s cancer.

item.title: Call for peace at Koroba secondary school ahead of national examinations
item.description: Teachers and students of Koroba Secondary have been called on to reconcile, forgive one another and unite in restoring peace at the school ahead of the Grade 10 and 12 National Examinations next month. Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu urged the students when he visited the school on Monday, 31st August to address a recent student strike and concerns raised by the school community.
item.content:encoded:
Teachers and students of Koroba Secondary have been called on to reconcile, forgive one another and unite in restoring peace at the school ahead of the Grade 10 and 12 National Examinations next month.

Hela Provincial Administrator Ronny Angu urged the students when he visited the school on Monday, 31st August to address a recent student strike and concerns raised by the school community.

As part of efforts to support the reconciliation process, Angu presented K10,000 to the school to prepare a special meal for students and teachers to share after the reconciliation ceremony.

“Students are our future. We cannot allow them to sit for their examinations without peace being restored. This reconciliation is important so our children can concentrate on their studies and perform well,” he said.

The PA also announced K40,000 in funding to provide meals for students throughout the examination period.

Meanwhile, the lack of reliable electricity has been identified as another major challenge affecting the school. To address the issue, Angu presented K100,000 to support the purchase of a new generator set.

“Our concern is you, the students. All we want from you is to focus on your education and make us proud by achieving top marks and gaining entry into tertiary institutions,” he said.

School Principal Stanley Langap thanked the Hela Provincial Government for the timely intervention, saying the assistance would help create a stable, peaceful and conducive learning environment for students as they prepare to sit their national examinations.

The school community is now expected to work together to restore harmony and ensure students can approach their examinations with peace of mind and confidence.

item.content:encoded:
The driver of a vehicle that was involved in a fatal hit-and-run incident in the early hours of Sunday, 23 August, 2026, along Madang's Modilon Road, has been charged with one count of wilful murder.

Provincial Police Commander, Superintendent Robert Baim revealed the suspect's name to be Eugene Makis, aged 34 from Sepa Villlage in Bogia District. He is a security supervisor with a security firm in Port Moresby.

According to initial police investigation, Makis was driving along the Modilon Road in the early hours of Sunday, between 1 and 2am, when he hit the deceased person from behind outside the Job Kai Bar.

"The driver had all the opportunities to avoid hitting the victim who was walking in the middle of the road. He was driving with high beams on. Also, there was sufficient lighting from shops within the vicinity, and the place was all lit up," PPC Baim said.

"He saw the victim walking and could have applied the brake to stop or swerve to either sides of the road as there were no oncoming vehicles at that time. It was the only vehicle on that particular stretch of the road at that time.

"The road was free, and the driver could have avoided the victim, but he did not. He had all the opportunities available to avoid hitting the victim but he did not use them.

"Investigators, therefore, believe it was intentional and so have charged the driver with wilful murder under section 229, sub section 1 of the Criminal Code Act."

Police further revealed that the victim, Roderick Hahambu, from Kubalia in the Yangoru-Sausia district of East Sepik, was at the Top Night Club on the night of the incident, however, left amidst an argument.

Supt Baim said the driver was also in the club at that time.

A post mortem on the body was conducted last Friday, which revealed the Late Roderick had his spleen ruptured, both his lungs burst, and the lower part of his right leg broken upon impact. He died on the spot due to the severity of injuries caused to his internal organs.

Roderick was an employee of PNG Power at the time of his death. He was a young linesman.

Baim said Makis has been refused police bail and will remain in custody until he appears before the Commital Court for mention.

"This is a serious case and police will not allow him bail. However, he can try to seek bail through the National Court," the Madang PPC said.

"As usual, a suspect is a suspect until proven guilty or otherwise by the court."

item.title: Telefomin hospital receives 15 new beds to serve more patients
item.description: Patients and families in Telefomin will now receive better care with 15 new hospital beds delivered to Telefomin Hospital this week. For the 79,000 people of Telefomin District, the donation addresses a critical need.
item.content:encoded:
Patients and families in Telefomin will now receive better care with 15 new hospital beds delivered to Telefomin Hospital this week.

For the 79,000 people of Telefomin District, the donation addresses a critical need.

The new beds will immediately increase the hospital’s capacity, meaning more sick mothers, children, and elders can be admitted and treated comfortably instead of waiting or sharing beds.

With limited beds, rural patients often travel long distances only to find no space. The additional 15 beds will reduce overcrowding in wards, improve patient comfort and recovery, allow faster admission for emergencies and maternity cases and support nurses and health workers to deliver better care

Valued at approximately K30,000 to K40,000, the beds represent a significant step toward stronger health services in one of PNG’s most remote hospitals.

Health workers at Telefomin Hospital say the timing is vital as patient numbers continue to grow.

Speaking at the handover, Acting General Manager of Teokyana Holdings Limited, Mr. Tammy Sinoksep said the company is committed to standing with the district.

“Teokyana Holdings Limited is for the 79,000 people of Telefomin. We are here to stay, and we will continue to support the district,” Sinoksep said.

He confirmed this is the first of more planned support for the rural people in Telefomin district.

item.title: District governance under scrutiny as DDA review starts
item.description: Public consultations reviewing the District Development Authority (DDA) Act 2014 are currently underway in Gulf, following complaints regarding public service delivery at the district level. A team from the Constitutional and Law Reform Commission (CLRC) arrived in the province this week to conduct a weeklong face-to-face legislative review.
item.content:encoded:
Public consultations reviewing the District Development Authority (DDA) Act 2014 are currently underway in Gulf, following complaints regarding public service delivery at the district level.

A team from the Constitutional and Law Reform Commission (CLRC) arrived in the province this week to conduct a weeklong face-to-face legislative review.

CLRC team leader Kenny Kaipas confirmed that Gulf is among eight provinces selected nationwide for the public exercise.

He said the DDA Act, enacted in 2014 to improve service delivery and empower local-level governments, had generated widespread concern across the country after ten years in operation.

“People across Papua New Guinea have raised serious issues regarding governance, lack of accountability, poor financial management, weak planning, procurement irregularities, and limited staffing capacity,” Kaipas said.

He said these concerns prompted Minister for Justice and Attorney-General Pila Niningi to direct the CLRC to undertake a comprehensive review of the legislation.

During the week, the CLRC delegation will meet with provincial and district management teams, district treasuries, public servants, community development officers, and local women and youth groups.

The public consultations are open to all community members and are being hosted at selected venues across Kerema town from Monday, Aug 31, to Thursday, Sept 3.

Participants and members of the public can also submit feedback digitally via an online consultation form accessible through a designated QR code provided during the sessions.

item.title: Govt agencies move to fast-track border post
item.description: Key government departments and border agencies met in Kiunga last week to fast-track the establishment of a temporary border post at Butmabin-Yetetkun in the North Fly district of Western. The initiative aims to secure fuel and essential supplies for Ok Tedi Mining Limited [OTML] as ongoing El Niño conditions severely disrupt standard logistics routes.
item.content:encoded:
Key government departments and border agencies met in Kiunga last week to fast-track the establishment of a temporary border post at Butmabin-Yetetkun in the North Fly district of Western.

The initiative aims to secure fuel and essential supplies for Ok Tedi Mining Limited [OTML] as ongoing El Niño conditions severely disrupt standard logistics routes.

The inter-agency meeting follows a directive issued on August 19 by the Department of Provincial and Local Level Government Affairs [DPLGA], which declared the operationalisation of the border post a national priority.

Representatives from the Western Provincial Administration convened alongside officials from DPLGA, Foreign Affairs, Lands and Physical Planning, Transport, PNG Immigration, PNG Customs, and PNG Biosecurity.

Under the framework, DPLGA will lead overall coordination, prepare the National Executive Council [NEC] submission, and conduct landowner awareness.

The Department of Foreign Affairs is tasked with leading government-to-government negotiations with Indonesia while supporting OTML’s talks with Indonesian state energy company Pertamina.

The Department of Lands and Physical Planning will execute land surveys and facilitate official gazettal of the site.

Concurrently, the Department of Transport is developing standard operating procedures (SOPs) for heavy transport vehicles, while Customs and Biosecurity will establish border control compliance protocols. Immigration officials will oversee travel documentation for all border operators.

Site surveys, agency deployments, customs protocol development, and landowner consultations were scheduled to run from Aug 24 to 30.

OTML stated that the temporary border post remains critical to maintaining mining operations and safeguarding national revenue during the prolonged dry spell.

Meanwhile, the Provincial Administrator and Mayor of Kiunga Town have reiterated FRPG’s position that the Butmabin site must not be used as a temporary border post. Speaking at Thursday’s meeting, both leaders said the focus must remain on the permanent gazetted site where work is ongoing.

item.title: Water level surge brings relief to North Fly
item.description: Fly River water levels at the Kiunga Wharf have surged following heavy rainfall in the headwaters, bringing relief to residents and businesses relying on river transport in North Fly.

item.title: National Literacy-Week launched in Northern province
item.description: The National Literacy Week was officially launched today, 31st August, in Northern Province to pave the way for government, schools, churches, communities, literacy practitioners and development partners to celebrate progress and discuss how literacy services can be improved in Papua New Guinea.
